newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't seeks to extend special budget fund.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't seeks to extend special budget fund.

text.p: The Brazilian government Friday said it would seek to extend the life of a 20-billion-real special budget fund because of the slow progress of fiscal reforms through Congress.
In a statement announcing a cost-cutting plan, the government also said it would issue a decree allowing for the elimination of 100,000 federal jobs, 73,000 of which are manned and the rest vacant.
In the statement, the ministers of finance, planning, social security and administration said they would send a constitutional amendment to Congress asking that the FEF budget be extended.
The FEF runs out at the end of the year and allows the government to spend 20 percent of the budget as it sees fit.

The ministers said the progress of pension, tax and civil service reforms through Congress was being affected by their "highly complex nature" and the fact that they represented "an important political and cultural break with the past".
"Given this scenario, we need to extend the FEF in order for there to be enough time to approve the constitutional reforms, their regulation and effective implementation," the ministers said.
The measures included cuts to public sector servant perks, measures to control spending by state firms and a decree allowing the government to cut 100,000 posts from its 560,000-strong payroll.
